skill.name: example-skill
skill.description: Template for documenting an AI skill with overview, trigger situations, protocol steps, examples, requirements, and related links.
skill.summary: Starter SKILL.md template for structuring AI skill documentation.
skill.author: ANcpLua

security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences in SKILL.md. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, network access, filesystem access, or real external command execution intent was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 24 opens a markdown fenced text block for protocol documentation. The backticks are formatting, not Ruby or shell execution syntax.
SKILL.md line 33 closes the protocol markdown fence and line 39 opens another text fence. These are documentation delimiters with no executable command context.
SKILL.md line 39 opens a markdown fenced text block for an example dialogue. The content is placeholder prose, not code that runs external commands.
SKILL.md line 42 closes the good example text fence and line 46 opens the bad example fence. The backticks only format documentation examples.
SKILL.md line 46 opens a markdown fenced text block for a non-executable bad example. No shell command, interpreter call, or user-controlled execution path is present.

content.value_statement: Starting a new AI skill is slow when the structure is unclear. This template gives authors a basic SKILL.md outline for overview, triggers, protocol, examples, requirements, and related links.
actual_capabilities: Provides front matter for a skill name and description.
Defines sections for overview, activation triggers, protocol, examples, requirements, and related resources.
Shows a three-step protocol format that authors can replace with real workflow steps.
Includes good and bad example sections for documenting expected assistant behavior.
Lists red flag prompts that remind authors to follow the documented protocol.
limitations: The skill is a placeholder and does not implement a domain-specific workflow.
All trigger situations, requirements, examples, and links must be replaced before production use.
It contains no scripts, tools, or automation beyond the markdown template.
It does not validate whether a finished skill follows marketplace quality rules.

use_cases.title: Draft a New Skill File
use_cases.description: Use the template as a starting structure when creating a new SKILL.md file.

use_cases.title: Teach Skill Structure
use_cases.description: Show contributors the core sections expected in a clear AI skill document.

use_cases.title: Review Documentation Coverage
use_cases.description: Compare a draft skill against the template sections to find missing guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Customize the Template
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new skill idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this example-skill template to draft a SKILL.md for [workflow]. Replace placeholders with concrete trigger situations, protocol steps, examples, requirements, and related links.

prompt_templates.title: Define Activation Triggers
prompt_templates.scenario: Clarify when the skill should be used.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my skill idea: [idea]. Write three clear situations where this skill should activate, using the template structure as the guide.

prompt_templates.title: Write Protocol Steps
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn a workflow into operational instructions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this workflow into a concise protocol section for SKILL.md: [workflow]. Include ordered steps and short details for each step.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Draft Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced readiness review before sharing a skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my customized SKILL.md against the example-skill structure. Identify missing sections, vague placeholders, weak examples, and unclear requirements.

output_examples.input: A user wants a starter skill for support ticket triage.
output_examples.output: A filled outline with a triage overview, activation triggers, step-by-step review protocol, good and bad response examples, requirements, and related resources.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks whether a draft skill still looks like a placeholder.
output_examples.output: A concise review noting which template sections remain generic and which sections need specific workflow details.

output_examples.input: A team lead wants to teach contributors how skills are organized.
output_examples.output: A section-by-section explanation of the template, focused on purpose, trigger clarity, protocol quality, examples, and requirements.

best_practices: Replace every placeholder with specific, testable guidance before publishing.
Keep trigger situations narrow so the skill activates only when useful.
Write examples that show both desired behavior and common mistakes.
anti_patterns: Publishing the template without replacing generic situations and requirements.
Using broad trigger language that makes the skill activate for unrelated tasks.
Adding protocol steps that require tools or permissions not documented in the skill.

faq.question: Is this a finished production skill?
faq.answer: No. It is a starter template that authors must customize for a real workflow.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it run commands or scripts?
faq.answer: No. The file contains markdown documentation only and no executable scripts.

faq.question: What should I replace first?
faq.answer: Replace the description, trigger situations, protocol steps, examples, requirements, and related links.

faq.question: Can reviewers use it as a checklist?
faq.answer: Yes. Reviewers can compare drafts against the included sections to find missing guidance.

faq.question: Why were backticks detected in the audit?
faq.answer: They are markdown fences around text examples, not shell commands or Ruby execution.
